Why is car insurance
so expensive?

lines.text: Car insurance prices jumped about 57% in four years.
lines.say: Car insurance prices jumped about fifty-seven percent in four years.

lines.text: And the reason isn't that you became a worse driver.
lines.say: And the reason isn't that you became a worse driver.

lines.text: Price data shows car insurance up 14.2% in 2022, then 20.3% in 2023.
lines.say: Price data shows car insurance up fourteen point two percent in twenty twenty-two, then twenty point three in twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: Then 11.3% in 2024 and 2.8% in 2025. Stacked, that's about 57%.
lines.say: Then eleven point three in twenty twenty-four and two point eight in twenty twenty-five. Stacked, that's about fifty-seven percent.

lines.text: Why? Insurers were losing money. In 2022, they paid out about $112 for every $100 of premium.
lines.say: Why? Insurers were losing money. In twenty twenty-two, they paid out about a hundred twelve dollars for every hundred of premium.

lines.text: Repairs got pricier, cars got packed with sensors, and claims got bigger.
lines.say: Repairs got pricier, cars got packed with sensors, and claims got bigger.

lines.text: So insurers raised rates until the math worked. By 2025, they paid out about $92 per $100.
lines.say: So insurers raised rates until the math worked. By twenty twenty-five, they paid out about ninety-two dollars per hundred.

lines.text: Now prices are easing: down 5.1% in the year to August 2026.
lines.say: Now prices are easing: down five point one percent in the year to August twenty twenty-six.

post.title: Why car insurance jumped about 57% in four years
post.ig:
Car insurance prices jumped about 57% in four years.
BLS price data: +14.2% in 2022, +20.3% in 2023, +11.3% in 2024, +2.8% in 2025 (December to December).
Why: insurers paid out about $112 per $100 of premium in 2022 as repairs and claims got pricier, then raised rates. By 2025 it was about $92.
Prices eased 5.1% in the year to August 2026, a small dip after a big climb.
Sources: BLS Consumer Price Index; Triple-I personal auto results.
